record.paper_title: SYMMETRY AND COLORINGS: SOME RESULTS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: Let ν(G) denote the minimal number of colors needed to color a group G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset, where a subset A of G is called symmetric if A = gA^{-1}g for some g in G. Determine ν(G) for non-commutative groups, and in particular decide whether ν(F₂) is finite for the free group F₂ on two generators.

evidence.quote: For a group G let ν(G) be the minimal number of colors necessary to color the group G so that G contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset.
1.2. Problem ( R.I.Grigorchuk). Investigate the invariant ν(G) for non-commutative groups. In particular, is ν(F2) finite, where F2 is the free group with two generators?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group. A subset $A\subseteq G$ is called symmetric if there exists $g\in G$ such that $A = gA^{-1}g$, i.e. $A$ is invariant under the involution $x\mapsto gx^{-1}g$. For a coloring $\chi:G	o\{1,2,\dots,r\}$, a subset $A\subseteq G$ is monochromatic if $\chi$ is constant on $A$. Define
$$
u(G)=\min\{r\in\mathbb{N} : 	ext{there exists } \chi:G	o\{1,\dots,r\} 	ext{ such that } G 	ext{ contains no infinite monochromatic symmetric subset}\},$$
with $
u(G)=\infty$ if no such finite $r$ exists.

(a) Determine $
u(G)$ for non-commutative groups $G$.

(b) In particular, let $F_2$ be the free group on two generators. Is $
u(F_2)$ finite?
artifact.status_search_result: The invariant ν(G) was introduced and studied for abelian groups (e.g. ν(Z^k)=k+1 by Banakh–Verbitsky–Vorobets), and the question of computing ν for non-commutative groups, in particular determining whether ν(F_2) is finite, was posed by R. I. Grigorchuk. Available web sources discuss the abelian case but provide no resolution for non-commutative groups or the free group F_2; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: A Ramsey Treatment of Symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Defines ν(G) and studies it for abelian groups, including ν(Z^k)=k+1.
status_evidence.claim: The invariant ν is well-studied for abelian groups but the non-commutative case, including ν(F_2), is left open.

status_evidence.title: Monochrome Symmetric Subsets in Colorings of Finite Abelian Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monochromatic symmetric subsets in colorings of finite abelian groups.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has focused on the abelian setting, with no published determination of ν(F_2).
